target_customer: Civil engineering firms, pipeline and district heating builders and utilities that must document open trenches
problem: Documenting underground infrastructure as built takes weeks of manual surveying and back-office planning.
business_model: B2B SaaS and per-project documentation, with paid pilots

founders.name: Julius Schilling
prior_employers: Aon (Chief of Staff to the CEO)
founders.background_notes: YC page and company site; YC page long description says insurance at Aon.

founders.name: Cornelius von Einem
education: ETH Zurich, PhD in robotics and computer vision (Autonomous Systems Lab)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built perception systems for railways and a wearable navigation system for blind users.

founders.name: Roger de Belsunce
education: University of Cambridge, PhD in astrophysics
founders.background_notes: Sources conflict on his title: academic advisor on the company site, professor in the launch post.

technical_complexity.rationale: Survey-grade 3D from smartphone video with automatic pipe and fitting identification is a computer vision research problem, and a 2021 study found smartphone video gave less consistent results.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary training data and accuracy claims of about 7 mm are hard to copy, but established vendors like Pix4D and Topcon sell trench capture workflows.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pix4D and Topcon market smartphone trench scanning (Topcon article dated June 2026); no acquisition of sizeless found.

market_need_then: Utilities and district heating builders need accurate as-built records, and the company reports seven paid pilots in three months with potential ACV of $1.4M, self reported.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found in a name search; the name has no stated meaning and is a coined negation.

pivots.from: ML model prototyping to production tooling and 3D digital twins for real estate (older YC and directory descriptions)
pivots.to: smartphone trench documentation for underground infrastructure
pivots.why: Not stated; derived from conflicting directory descriptions, so the dates are approximate.

outcome_analysis: sizeless focused on underground infrastructure documentation after earlier positioning that varied across directories, and reports paid pilots with German utilities and builders. No funding or independent traction data was found, so its stage beyond YC is unknown.
notes: No funding found; the funding search returned only unrelated companies. The outcome search for sizeless returned nothing about the company (SiteScan results belong to SiteScape, unrelated). Competitor evidence is June 2026 and earlier academic work, not dated near the batch, so the list is empty. Location conflicts between San Francisco, New York and Zurich across sources. Pivot is inferred from directory descriptions and flagged low confidence.
